description: Capability for the main window. Notes: opener:allow-open-path exists for the attachments feature (src/services/attachments/file-actions.ts) — opening downloaded/cache files with the OS default app. It is path-scoped to $APPDATA/** (the attachment cache subtree the feature actually opens); the mock/dev note that it 'cannot be narrowed' is outdated — tauri-plugin-opener supports path scopes and every openPath call site targets <appData>/attachment_cache. http:default is limited to the Google API hosts the Gmail REST client calls (token-manager.ts, gmail-api.ts, add-gmail.ts) plus www.virustotal.com for the opt-in attachment malware hash lookup (src/services/attachments/malware-lookup.ts — hash-only GETs, no content upload); the OAuth authorization URL is opened in the system browser, not via plugin-http. The https://* entry exists for the RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe POST (task 18.3, security/unsubscribe.ts): its targets are List-Unsubscribe URLs owned by arbitrary mailing-list servers, so the host set is unbounded by design — the request itself is user-initiated, form-encoded (`List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`), and carries no credentials or message content. sql:default is read-only (close/load/select); sql:allow-execute is required because the DB layer writes (migrations, message ingestion, settings) through database.execute — without it every write is ACL-denied in the packaged app (the mock harness masks this by replacing plugin-sql). fs:allow-open exists for data portability (tasks 19.2–19.4): the mbox exporter streams through a plugin-fs file handle (`open`, src/services/data-portability/mbox.ts) — its sibling write commands (write/remove) already ride fs:allow-appdata-write-recursive's write-all set, but `open` sits in the fs command model's read family and needs this permission. The command stays path-scope-gated at runtime — the dialog plugin adds every picked/saved path to the fs scope for the session (unpersisted; see @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog dist-js) — so no $HOME scope is granted. The import parser reads picked .eml/.mbox files Rust-side (mail_import.rs std::fs) and needs no fs permission at all.
